races.name: 100% Racingtv Profits Back To Racing Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Flightofthephoenix
runners_data.note: Prominent racer on the back of two consecutive wins, both on soft or similar ground at 11-12f, making this trip and conditions squarely in his favour; Charles Hills yard firing with 3 wins from 21 in 14 days and son James Hills claiming 5lb, giving a meaningful weight advantage at 159lbs.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins make Flightofthephoenix hard to ignore, though a seventh two starts further back and a light turnaround of six days may test her stamina for the effort; she has run over today's trip and steps up from stall 11 carrying 159 lb.

runners_data.name: I'd Go Maniac
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with a win and a place in 15 soft-ground runs, proven over 12f at Goodwood, and Alan King's yard is live with 1 from 11 in 14 days; hg:p (hood) suggests a horse that can sometimes get lit up, so early energy management on a pressured pace is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Winning last time out and boasting experience over today's trip, I'd Go Maniac arrives in solid nick after 31 days off, with our rating of 72 lending further encouragement; the main risk is whether he can build on that victory under 156 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Ribble River
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who needs to come from off the pace, and while soft ground poses no concern, her last five starts have been over 16-17f at Goodwood where she never landed a blow; the step back to 11.5f is a query, though Lizzie Quinlan's yard is freshening with 1 from 3 in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Ribble River showed he can win at this level, a winner two starts back, though he was only third last time out after 47 days off; he has run over today's trip and going, but 155 lb from stall 12 makes life no easier for a horse our rating suggests is slightly below par here.

runners_data.name: Austrian Theory
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose recent form figures (9,7,5,8,5) show consistency without a win, and soft ground is untested in his last five starts (all Good or Standand); Tim Easterby's yard is busy but not sharp (9 from 87 in 14 days), and the 17-day break is neutral.
runners_data.comment: Austrian Theory arrives here in good heart after a 17-day break, and his experience over today's trip and conditions stands him in good stead; third last time out is the clear form highlight, and our rating of 78 marks him as the one to beat in this field, even if he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Roland Garros
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing a tongue-tie, most likely to push hardest for the lead against Alpine Sierra and Star Start over this stamina-testing trip; his last five starts show a top-of-the-ground bias and no soft-ground wins, so his ability to sustain a forceful gallop on this surface is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back gives Roland Garros a foothold in the argument, but he has finished seventh twice in his last six starts and our rating of 62 sits below his official mark, suggesting he may need to find improvement; he has run over today's trip and returns on a handy 16-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Progressive front-runner who won back-to-back and has three wins in his last six, though all five recent runs were on Good ground and there is a legitimate soft-going query; as the most naturally enthusiastic pace-setter at OR=64, he risks burning out in a three-way battle before the stamina test truly begins.
runners_data.comment: A hat-trick of wins sits deep in his recent form, but a fifth and a ninth since make him hard to trust, and our rating ranks him tenth of thirteen in this field. Has run over today's trip and going, and 38 days between runs leaves fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Revelio
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose sole soft-ground start produced a 10th, and his best form (2nd, 4th) has come on Good; stepping up significantly in trip from 8-10f to 11.5f is the main concern, with no evidence of genuine staying ability over this distance yet.
runners_data.comment: Revelio comes into this off a 28-day break with experience over today's trip, and he shaped with promise when second three starts back, but he has been winless in his last five starts and his ranking of ninth of thirteen suggests he faces a stiff task from stall six.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with recent soft-ground starts (4th, 5th over 10-11f), giving him fitness and going experience over rivals who have been off longer; three days since last run is unusually quick and Philip Kirby's 14-day record (2/10) is modest, but soft ground and the step up in trip suit his grinding style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and back out just three days ago, Spirit Catcher carries 148 lb from stall 13, though he has run over today's trip and going before; a second six starts back offers the sole recent encouragement, and his rating of 67 suggests a shade of untapped potential.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form with two wins from six (including on soft at 10f), and though her natural instinct is to race from hold-up, she has been redistributed to midfield on this map because there are simply too many true closers for the race shape to accommodate; the going and form are right but securing clear passage through a 13-runner field in amateur company is the tactical risk.
runners_data.comment: Recobella has winning form in her recent starts — a winner last time out and a winner three starts back — but her rating of 56 leaves her ranked 12 of 13 on these figures, and that gulf in class makes her hard to fancy despite the experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has run 3 days ago, bringing fitness but raising a slight freshness query; her record is a string of placed efforts (2,2,1,2,3) suggesting she runs her race every time, and she will make the pace genuine from the off, though sustaining it on Soft ground over this trip against two rivals doing the same is a significant stamina ask.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Star Start is hard to fancy at the weights despite a run of placed efforts — second two of his last three starts, and a winner three starts back — but a stone-cold cold trainer strike-rate of 0 from 20 in the past fortnight is the biggest turn-off.

runners_data.name: Shahbaz
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose recent form (8,2,4,6,6,6) does not inspire confidence, and while his tongue-tie was removed in the last run, he has been slotted into midfield on the map simply because there are more closers than the pace scenario can accommodate at the back; soft-ground debut in this form makes him hard to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Shahbaz's rating of 68 puts him well clear of his official mark and flags him as a serious threat at the weights, and his experience over today's trip and going is a genuine asset from stall seven; the concern is a run of three consecutive sixth-place finishes that leaves him yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Cavalry Call
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer whose last five starts read 11,13,7,9 with a blank — poor form that makes even his natural running style hard to back; he too is shown in midfield by necessity rather than intention, and with 0 wins or places from 15 similar-going runs the evidence does not support revival here.
runners_data.comment: Cavalry Call has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating puts him well clear of his official mark, suggesting he is significantly better than he has shown in recent starts; the risk is a winless run of five that includes no better than seventh.

runners_data.name: Red Derek
runners_data.note: A decade-old prominent racer whose 11 runs in similar going have produced 0 wins and 5 places, and 81 days off is the longest absence in the field; Lisa Williamson's small yard (1/3 in 14 days) and the top weight for age concerns suggest this is a confidence run rather than a winning attempt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Red Derek makes this a tough assignment; he has run over today's distance and going before, and stall three is his draw, but there is little else in the bare form to inspire confidence after 81 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Roland Garros, Alpine Sierra, and Star Start are all confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the outset over 1m3½f on Soft ground at Haydock, making a strong, searching gallop almost inevitable. The prolonged battle for supremacy up front will stretch the field early, turning this into a thorough stamina examination on testing ground — a combination that can burn out even genuinely pace-suited horses before the home straight. Prominent racers who can settle just off the hot pace without expending excess energy — rather than true hold-up horses who will lose significant ground — are best placed to capitalise when the leaders inevitably tire in the closing stages. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Roland Garros (tongue-tie), Alpine Sierra, and Star Start are most likely to actually force their way to the front, while Recobella, Shahbaz, and Cavalry Call, all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield in the map, are unlikely to get the late run they need given the pace will be honest rather than suicidal. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours a prominent racer with soft-ground stamina who can track the burning pace and pick up the pieces, rather than a closer having to make up ground on a tired but still-galloping rail.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners push each other along at a strong pace and a prominent tracker conserves energy to strike at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The brutal three-way battle for the lead on Soft ground will have the pacemakers weakening inside the final quarter-mile, leaving a prominent horse who has travelled smoothly just off the pace with a decisive advantage. Flightofthephoenix (recent soft-ground wins, in-form Charles Hills yard) and I'd Go Maniac (proven AW/turf versatility, decent soft form) are ideally profiled to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters — most likely Alpine Sierra or Star Start — establishes a lead and the others either back off or are outpaced from the start.
scenarios.body: In this shape the anticipated pace battle never fully ignites, allowing a single front-runner to control tempo, conserve enough to keep finding, and hold on through the Soft ground stamina test. Alpine Sierra's hat-trick form and soft-ground switching, or Star Start's consistent placed record and recent fitness (3 days ago), make both viable beneficiaries of this less-contested scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other out so completely that a late-running hold-up horse can pick off the stragglers from the rear.
scenarios.body: This shape requires the genuine hold-up horses — Recobella (won twice recently, strong soft form) and Ribble River (hold-up operator, soft ground fine) — to be positioned further back than natural in a congested midfield, making a clear run difficult and reducing the scenario's probability. If they do find daylight, Recobella's recent winning form and Ribble River's staying profile give them a fighting chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine but not suicidal and a resolute midfield stayer simply outstays rivals in the Soft ground closing stages.
scenarios.body: Austrian Theory has soft-ground placed form and a thorough stayer's profile over this trip, while Spirit Catcher has recent soft-ground starts and the fitness edge of a 3-day turnaround. This outcome needs the pace to sustain rather than suddenly collapse, rewarding a relentless galloping type rather than a change-of-gear horse.

watchPoints.text: Roland Garros, Alpine Sierra, and Star Start could engage in a suicidal three-way pace battle from the jump — monitor which of the three blinks first in the opening two furlongs, as any capitulation will dramatically reshape the race.

Alpine Sierra has never won or placed on Soft ground (all five recent runs on Good) — if conditions are riding genuinely Soft rather than transitional, watch for him to come off the bridle earlier than expected and surrender the lead prematurely.

Recobella is in fine recent form but will be racing from a position further forward than her natural hold-up style demands — if she gets boxed in behind a wall of tiring front-runners in the final two furlongs, her finishing effort could be fatally compromised.

Flightofthephoenix is fresh off back-to-back wins with the in-form Hills combination — watch for him to be ridden prominently with intent to track the pace rather than chase it, which would be the ideal tactical execution in this race shape.

Spirit Catcher ran only three days ago — watch his pre-race demeanour and early movement in the race; if he travels sweetly through the Soft ground in midfield without over-racing, his recent fitness edge over rivals who have been off 17-47 days could be significant.

races.name: Jackie Harbridge In Loving Memory Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Bailey Partnership Celebrating 50 Years Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tribal Appearance
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up filly who ran 2nd on soft over 6f at Firm latest, with simulated soft form showing just one placing from three; 90-day absence is a concern and Jack Doughty's claim adds an unknown element.|
runners_data.comment: Tribal Appearance has placed second in recent starts and, carrying 135 lb from stall four, brings solid each-way claims after running over today's trip; the chief concern is that he heads here 90 days fresh and remains yet to win in his last three outings.

runners_data.name: Koodini
runners_data.note: Ran 12th on soft over 7f last time but has a win and two placings on good-to-soft/soft variants over 6f, suggesting that run may be forgiven; David Probert rides and Hugo Palmer's recent 3/35 form is modest, but this horse has the most credible soft-ground profile among the closers.|
runners_data.comment: Koodini arrives here on the back of a win two starts back and has run over today's trip, with 14 days since that last outing suggesting he's turned up fit; the concern is that unplaced return means he must bounce back to his best to threaten.

runners_data.name: Vinery
runners_data.note: Placed over 6f on good at Goodwood but has yet to encounter soft ground; Charles Bishop takes the ride for the Greenall/Guerriero yard who are 1/10 in 14 days, and a step up in trip from 6f debut efforts is unproven.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Vinery's best recent effort was a second two starts back, though a seventh last time out and a ranking of tenth of twelve on our figures make him hard to fancy here despite the distance experience and a 28-day break.

runners_data.name: High Hazard
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes — a significant concern on soft ground over 7f; has placed twice on good-to-firm over 8f but soft form on this trip is uninspiring (13th and 9th in two tries), and the Hugo Palmer yard's 14-day record offers limited confidence.|
runners_data.comment: High Hazard shaped with promise when third three starts back and second four starts back, and he returns on a quick 14-day turnaround with experience over today's trip; the risk is that he has been unplaced in both subsequent outings and remains yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Katie's Cavalier
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and pace-setter, though her STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) cautions that she is somewhat racing out of role as an ostensibly prominent type pushed into a true lead position; her sole win came over 7f on good at Goodwood and soft ground is untested, but her control of this race's tempo is her primary weapon.|
runners_data.comment: Katie's Cavalier is the clear pick on recent form, winning last time out 25 days ago and returning here in good order; he has run over today's trip and faces this on 131 lb from stall nine, with our rating of 80 underscoring his appeal.

runners_data.name: Gerry's Darling
runners_data.note: Strong recent form including a win at Goodwood and a 2nd over 7f on good, all on a right-handed track; Clifford Lee is reliable and Roger Fell's yard is 2/9 in 14 days — notably hasn't raced on soft but the stamina-laden form over 7f makes this a strong candidate in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out following a win two starts back, Gerry's Darling arrives in decent nick on 27 days' rest and has run over today's trip, though 130 lb from stall 11 is no small ask for a filly rated 69 officially.

runners_data.name: Green Titan
runners_data.note: Has placed on soft over 6f (2nd at Chelmsford) and on soft over 5f, so the going is not a concern; stepping up to 7f for the first time is the key question, and Pat Cosgrave's experience here helps George Boughey's 4/32 14-day string.|
runners_data.comment: Green Titan returns after 17 days, and his second three starts back hints at ability, yet he has been winless in recent starts and a sixth two starts back tempers enthusiasm; experience over today's trip and going at least ensures no unknowns on those fronts.

runners_data.name: Diplomata
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lightly raced colt has placed three times from three starts, all on good or good-to-soft; Tom Marquand takes the ride, but his true running style is hold-up — pushed into midfield by congestion at the rear, he may not get the clean, late run his form suggests he needs.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Diplomata has nonetheless shown consistency with a third last time out and has run over today's trip, though carrying 129 lb from stall eight and a speed rating of 66 suggest she faces a stiff task splitting the field.

runners_data.name: Peggy's Lad
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at Southwell (Standard) and has placed at 8f, so stamina is not a worry; David Allan knows this horse and Iain Jardine's 3/21 recent form is respectable, though all career form has come on good or standard surfaces and soft ground is an unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Peggy's lad ranks last on our figures and is hard to fancy on that basis, though he does arrive on the back of a win two starts ago and has run over today's trip, giving him something to build on at least.

runners_data.name: Greek Street
runners_data.note: All four career runs have come on good or standard surfaces — soft ground here is genuinely unproven; Sean Levey rides for Harry Eustace's yard (2/16 in 14 days), and his natural hold-up style means he is squeezed into midfield by the volume of closers in this field, limiting his scope.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Greek Street faces a stiff task here; a second three starts back offers some encouragement, but back-to-back sixths since then, carrying 127 lb from stall 12, make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: One Shot Kodi
runners_data.note: Three runs on standard or good surfaces without a win, and steps up to 7f turf for the first time; Tom Eaves is a reliable northern claimer and Kevin Ryan's 3/36 14-day record is active, but soft ground and the trip are both unexplored territory.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, One Shot Kodi at least has experience over today's trip and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround, but a fourth last time out represents her best recent effort and she faces a stiff task from a rating of 66.

runners_data.name: Unbeatable Fame
runners_data.note: Placed 3rd over 6f on good for Richard & Peter Fahey (6/49 in 14 days, active yard), but this is a step up in trip and the horse's natural rear-of-field style is compressed into a midfield map position by the sheer volume of hold-up types — Oisin McSweeney faces a significant challenge finding daylight.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Unbeatable Fame faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip before and a third two starts back offers a crumb of comfort; 17 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough.

races.paceDynamic: Katie's Cavalier is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner nursery handicap and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to pressure her — Gerry's Darling, Green Titan, Peggy's Lad, and One Shot Kodi are prominent types who will likely settle just behind her rather than contest the lead. On soft ground over 7f at Haydock, a flat course, that uncontested lead at a sustainable clip is a significant tactical advantage, likely producing a true but not brutal gallop that keeps prominent runners travelling within their comfort zone. The hold-up battalion is overcrowded: Tribal Appearance, Koodini, Vinery, and High Hazard are natural closers, while Diplomata, Greek Street, and Unbeatable Fame are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear positions are simply too congested — their ability to switch off and deliver a sustained late run will be compromised by the traffic and the soft ground's attrition. The race shape strongly favours the prominent group sitting just behind Katie's Cavalier, as the pace is controlled rather than dawdling, the ground will stretch the field, and late closers face the dual burden of soft ground stamina demands and a race unlikely to be truly run away from them at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Katie's Cavalier sets a controlled, uncontested pace and the prominent chasers travel smoothly just behind throughout the 7f.
scenarios.body: The soft ground and flat Haydock track reward horses who travel prominently without expending early energy fighting for position; Gerry's Darling, Green Titan, and Peggy's Lad all sit in the slipstream and have the stamina to sustain their challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely steady early and Katie's Cavalier simply builds an unassailable lead in the soft ground that rivals cannot close.
scenarios.body: A lone leader on a flat track in soft going can exploit rivals who burn energy grinding through the ground in pursuit; Katie's Cavalier's recent Goodwood win over 7f demonstrates she can see out the trip when conditions suit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the genuine closers — Koodini or Tribal Appearance — get a clean passage to unleash a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Soft ground accentuates the difference between those who conserve energy and those who burn it early; Koodini has placed on soft before over 7f and has the form credentials to capitalise if rivals tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If Diplomata, Greek Street, or Unbeatable Fame manage to find clear running from their compressed midfield berths and produce the sustained finish their true hold-up style requires.
scenarios.body: This scenario is discounted because all three are natural rear-of-field types forced into a midfield role they are unlikely to fully exploit in a soft-ground race where ground is covered efficiently at the front; the style mismatch and traffic concerns make a clean late delivery improbable.

watchPoints.text: Katie's Cavalier's soft-ground stamina is unproven — if she ties up in the final furlong having set the pace alone, the prominent group immediately behind her (Gerry's Darling, Green Titan) are perfectly placed to sweep past.

High Hazard is flagged as a horse that fades in finishes — if Sam James attempts to push forward from a hold-up position on soft ground, watch for this runner weakening badly in the closing stages and potentially interfering with others coming through.

Diplomata, Greek Street, and Unbeatable Fame are all genuine hold-up horses jostling in a congested midfield — monitor the early stages for potential bunching or shuffling back that could cost them any realistic chance of getting a run.

Gerry's Darling has not raced on soft ground in any of his career starts — his Goodwood form is solid but all on a drying surface; any significant deterioration in going could shift the balance toward those with proven soft credentials like Koodini or Green Titan.

The Haydock 7f on soft is a stamina-sapping test — runners dropping back from 8f (Vinery, High Hazard) may have an advantage in terms of trip exposure, but horses without any soft-ground experience at all (Gerry's Darling, Peggy's Lad, One Shot Kodi) carry a meaningful unknown into this ground profile.

races.name: Ebf Ashton In Makerfield Novice Stakes
Reprocolor Premier Ebf Fillies' Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Lady Roisia
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly holds the highest OR in the race at 90 and has a soft-ground win on her card, but her recent form includes an U (unseated) and she steps back up to 1m2f after a 61-day break; she is the confirmed pace setter and her ability to control the tempo unchallenged is her biggest asset today.

runners_data.name: Miss Tonnerre
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old returns after 99 days off, a notably long absence, and her hold-up style requires genuine pace to chase down; her soft-going record across nine runs yields no wins and no places, which is a significant concern on today's conditions despite her ability to stay the trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Miss Tonnerre nevertheless heads the ratings and shaped with promise in patches, has run over today's trip and going, and a 99-day break may have freshened her; the 134 lb burden is the one thing to overcome.

runners_data.name: Hoseki
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old has won three of her last four starts, all on good ground, and steps into soft conditions for the first time — her form is progressive and she will travel prominently, but the going switch is the key unknown against more battle-hardened soft-ground operators.
runners_data.comment: Hoseki has won three of her last five starts and arrives on the back of a win two runs back, with experience of both today's trip and going working in her favour; the fourth last time out is the one blot to keep onside.

runners_data.name: Star Cast
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's four-year-old arrives on a remarkable run of form showing 2-1-1-1-2 in her last five, all on soft, and her trainer has had no winners in the past 14 days; she travels prominently and loves this ground, making her the standout soft-ground specialist in the field.
runners_data.comment: Star Cast has won three times in her last six starts, was a winner two starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going makes her a genuine threat at 131 lb — the second last time out keeps her rolling into this, though her draw at stall three is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Hollywell Stream
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's three-year-old won on good ground last time over 1m2f and has placed on soft previously, giving her credible each-way claims as a hold-up type; she needs the pace to be genuinely taxing to bring her late run into play, and Callum Shepherd will need to judge the pace correctly from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Hollywell Stream arrives on the back of a win last time out, has experience of today's distance and going, and her 89 rating underlines a strong claims here from stall one carrying 130 lb — the chief risk is whether that weight blunts her late effort.

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's four-year-old has won on soft and her form figures show 1-2-1-2 pattern of consistency, but she is a true hold-up runner who has been pushed into a midfield slot on the pace map because the rear positions are crowded — her style-fit score of 0.92 flags that she is unlikely to get the race run to suit her in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Polygram faces a stiff ask here, though her recent form reads well — a winner last time out and two wins in her last six starts — and she has run over today's trip before, returning on a quick 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old has placed consistently but never wins away from home or on soft ground, and as a naturally prominent racer she has been displaced into a midfield position on the map because Star Cast and Hoseki are the more forceful prominent types; the 5lb claimer Lauren Young adds a minor weight benefit but the style compromise and going record make this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Geo is yet to score despite placing regularly, and ranked sixth of seven on our figures she faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going, and 26 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh enough.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Roisia is the confirmed front runner and will control this from the front, setting a sustainable gallop on soft ground over 1m2f at Haydock with no serious pressure to her outside. Hoseki and Star Cast are both prominent types who will track closely behind, meaning the first two positions are occupied by genuine pace horses, creating a true-run but not suicidal tempo that is likely to reward those who can travel strongly in the first half of the race. Hold-up mares Miss Tonnerre and Hollywell Stream will need the pace to genuinely stretch the field before their finishing effort becomes meaningful, which on soft ground over this trip is plausible but demands things go right. The field contains more prominent types than can all occupy forward positions — Geo and Polygram are genuine prominent and hold-up runners respectively who have been mapped to midfield because Star Cast and Hoseki are likely to claim those slots ahead of them, meaning both face a compromised race shape relative to their natural style. This race shape — a single front runner with a small chasing pack — strongly favours prominent hold types who can sit just off Lady Roisia and deploy their finish from a position of control, rather than late closers who must make up ground on a testing surface.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Roisia leads comfortably and Hoseki or Star Cast track in a close second, with the pace honest but not brutal on the soft.
scenarios.body: Lady Roisia dictates a controlled tempo that stretches the hold-up horses without inviting them into the race, and the first three home are drawn from those who travel prominently and have the stamina to maintain their effort through the testing ground; soft-ground form is pivotal here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to thoroughly empty the prominent runners in the final two furlongs, leaving late closers with real momentum.
scenarios.body: Miss Tonnerre or Hollywell Stream, having been delivered late, find the front pair tying up on the soft and surge past on the run to the line; Hollywell Stream's recent win and soft-going experience makes her the more credible of the two hold-up types.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Roisia finds an uncontested lead and the pace is too gentle to enable any finisher, allowing her to dictate and control the closing stages.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to push Lady Roisia, she settles into a rhythm that suits her stamina profile and the soft ground does not take its toll before the line; her OR of 90 is the highest in the field and her soft-going win on the form string backs this up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Geo or Polygram into midfield actually suits them and the pace collapses into the final furlong, opening a gap for an unexpected finisher.
scenarios.body: Polygram, a genuine hold-up type who has won on soft and over this trip range, could find the position less compromising than anticipated and deliver a late run if the prominent runners hit the wall; Geo's prominent nature means this is a less natural fit and the style-fit discount applies heavily.

watchPoints.text: Star Cast is the standout soft-ground specialist with 2W+5P from 15 starts on soft and arrives here in career-best form — if she tracks Lady Roisia prominently and gets a clear run, she is the biggest danger to market principals.

Hoseki has never raced on soft ground and drops into it having won three in a row on good — watch the market for any drift that signals connections or punters have reservations about the going switch.

Miss Tonnerre's 99-day absence combined with a 0W0P record on soft in nine attempts represents a significant compounding of concerns — if she weakens early it may affect the gaps available to Hollywell Stream in the closing stages.

Lady Roisia has an unseated rider in recent form and returns after 61 days; any sign of reluctance to settle or anxiety in the stalls could disrupt the expected pace map and compress the field, potentially changing the tempo entirely.

Polygram and Geo are both racing out of their natural positions due to the redistribution — if either manages to creep into a more forward slot in the early stages, the pace dynamic changes and the hold-up horses lose the strong pace they need.

races.name: Visit Racingtv.com Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Sharp Move
runners_data.note: William Haggas in strong form (9 wins from 49 in 14 days) and the horse has a genuine soft-ground win on its record, but a hold-up style at Haydock 1m2f with 14 runners means it must pass a lot of horses; last run 6 days ago is a neutral factor and the form string shows inconsistency.|
runners_data.comment: Sharp Move won three starts back but has finished eighth in each of his last two outings, which clouds his chance here; he has run over today's trip and carries 138 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Freddie Steady Go
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after an 82-day absence for a yard with just 2 runners in the period; one soft-ground win exists over 7f but the jump to 12f and first run for nearly three months on testing ground is a significant combination of risks.|
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back, Freddie Steady Go brings strong claims here as the top-rated runner in the field, and he has experience of today's going; the 82-day absence is the one query, though 138 lb from stall four is workable.

runners_data.name: Nightsinwhitesatin
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent prominent-racing type who has finished second five times in six recent starts over exactly this trip at Goodwood — a switch to Haydock's more galloping soft terrain is a new question, but the 5lb claimer Cian Horgan keeps costs down and the horse's stamina at 12f is beyond doubt.|
runners_data.comment: Nightsinwhitesatin has been a model of consistency, finishing second in four of her last five starts, and has experience of today's trip and going — the main concern is whether she can finally convert that placed form into a winning one after 48 days off.

runners_data.name: Mehmas Champion
runners_data.note: Out-and-out hold-up horse who will not secure its natural position given the number of rear-rankers in the field; the form string includes several zeros and the horse fades in finishes, making its chances marginal unless the race sets up perfectly, which it is unlikely to do.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Mehmas Champion is hard to fancy, though he has been freshened up on an 18-day break and does carry his 135 lb from a manageable draw of six.

runners_data.name: High Point
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on soft at Musselburgh and the trainer Iain Jardine has three winners in 14 days, but this is a genuine off-the-pace runner being squeezed into a midfield berth it does not want — distance form gives hope but style displacement tempers confidence sharply.|
runners_data.comment: High Point won four starts back and was third six starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and going to call upon; however, three consecutive unplaced efforts since that victory make his current form the chief concern.

runners_data.name: It'sneverjustone
runners_data.note: Prominent racer dropping back from 7f to 10f but stepping up to 12f here, which is a clear stamina unknown; four recent finishes of 4-4-6-5 show consistency without winning, and the Loughnane yard has no wins from 14 recent runners.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and unplaced most recently, It'sneverjustone does at least bring going experience to the table and steps back out after a 37-day break, though his ranking of seventh of fourteen suggests he faces a stiff task from stall eight carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Has placed prominently in her headgear at 10f on good ground but soft 12f is a step into the unknown; displaced further back than her natural style suits, and the form line showing a win over 10f on good ground is not obviously transferable to today's conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Pearl Eye won three starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, but sixth last time out suggests he is a little short of his best right now; 134 lb from stall 11 gives connections something to weigh up, though 24 days off may have freshened him.

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner who will get an uncontested lead — the key question is whether a horse who has finished 9th and 7th in its last two 10f starts can last home over 12f on soft having done all the donkey work; the form suggests this trip is the ceiling of its stamina.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eleventh of fourteen on our figures, Pomme Pomme faces a stiff task, though a return to today's trip and a third two starts back offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Pol Roger
runners_data.note: Placed on soft at 10f and has gone 1-2-3 in his last three 10f starts — this is the first attempt at 12f and that is the one genuine concern, but the prominent style, the returning claimer Rhys Elliott and the consistent form make him an obvious candidate in the most likely race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Pol Roger franked his recent winning form with victory last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and going in his favour; the weight of 133 lb and a ranking of tenth of fourteen in the field are the steadying factors here.

runners_data.name: Arcadian Nights
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran who races prominently and has been consistently mid-pack in recent finishes (4-5-6); no wins since 2022 and a form history confined to good and standard going means soft ground is an unresolved question for this horse.|
runners_data.comment: Arcadian Nights brings experience of today's trip and conditions, and a rating of 90 makes him a leading threat at the weights, carrying 133 lb from stall ten; the main concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Knight Of Glory
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's three-year-old has a headgear note suggesting he has been best when switched off; 68 days off the track is a concern, and although a prominent or hold-up type, he will be in a midfield berth today and needs to prove his soft-ground credentials after a string of good-ground runs.|
runners_data.comment: Knight Of Glory has managed one win in his last five starts and arrives here 68 days since his last outing, which adds to the concern; rated 72 on our figures and ranked last of the 14 runners, he faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's trip and carries a workable weight.

runners_data.name: Blue To Blue
runners_data.note: Ruth Jefferson yard has been quiet (no winners in 14 days) and this three-year-old is a natural hold-up horse whose preference for sitting last will be frustrated by the field's composition; form at up to 10f on good ground does not shout 12f soft.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Blue To Blue did show a flash of ability when third two runs back, and he has run over today's trip; carrying 130 lb from stall 13, he holds a slight edge over his official mark but that unplaced latest effort gives pause.

runners_data.name: Night Patrol
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on soft at Nottingham which is a clear positive, but has not raced for 90 days and the step to 12f is substantial; a hold-up horse with a soft-ground pedigree who needs a truly run race to land a blow from his natural position.|
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and a winner four starts back, Night Patrol brings some proven ability to the table, but unplaced last time and off for 90 days raises freshness questions; the 130 lb burden is no help either.

runners_data.name: Storm Point
runners_data.note: Won both career races on soft or standard-to-soft surfaces and Ed Walker's yard is in form; races prominently and a 1m2f trip looks well within range as he steps up from shorter — the going is a genuine asset and this runner looks well placed positionally to be involved.|
runners_data.comment: Storm Point has won twice in his last five starts, including a win two starts back, but ranked 12 of 14 on our figures and a last-run seventh makes him difficult to fancy, though 56 days off leaves condition an open question.

races.paceDynamic: Pomme Pomme is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will dictate a controlled, unchallenged gallop on soft ground over 1m2f at Haydock — a track that rewards handy positions and punishes horses who give too much ground away early. Nightsinwhitesatin, Pol Roger, Storm Point, It'sneverjustone and Arcadian Nights will press forward into the prominent berths, creating a compact early order with Pomme Pomme setting an honest but manageable tempo on soft ground that will stretch stamina without producing a true meltdown pace. The field contains more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate naturally — Blue To Blue, Mehmas Champion, High Point, Pearl Eye and Knight Of Glory are all genuine rear-rankers who will be shuffled into midfield rather than their preferred last-of-all position, meaning they will need to travel better through the race than their form histories suggest they are capable of. This race shape — a lone leader, a sustained soft-ground stamina test and a press of prominent horses immediately behind — strongly favours runners who can race in the first three or four and sustain their gallop, giving the prominent-to-midfield profile the decisive edge over closers who will find soft Haydock ground an unforgiving return journey from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pomme Pomme Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Pomme Pomme gets an uncontested lead and sets a steady-to-honest soft-ground gallop that stretches hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Pomme Pomme settles in front without pressure, the prominent pack of Nightsinwhitesatin, Pol Roger and Storm Point track closely, and the race becomes a stamina examination in the straight where horses close to the pace hold their positions to the line. Nightsinwhitesatin's consistency at 12f on similar ground and Pol Roger's recent form over this course and distance give them first call; Storm Point's soft-ground win is also directly relevant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Overwhelms Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent horses quickens past Pomme Pomme early in the straight and the race becomes a duel between handy types.
scenarios.body: Pol Roger or Storm Point hit the front turning in, forcing a true battle in the final two furlongs that punishes anything held up further back; soft ground ensures the winning margin is decisive and the race is run out fully by the eventual winner. Storm Point's 1-from-1 on soft and Pol Roger's placed record over C&D make them the standout beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely searching through the middle stages and horses held in mid-division benefit from the collapse of the prominent pack.
scenarios.body: A truly run race on heavy-ish soft ground sometimes sees prominent horses empty before the line, allowing a horse like Knight Of Glory or Sharp Move — who will be closer than ideal but still with more reserves than true front-runners — to pick up the pieces. Sharp Move's Haggas yard is in good form and the horse showed clear soft-going aptitude when winning at Salisbury, giving this scenario its slim but real thread of plausibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fierce and the true rear-guarders manage to find clear daylight late despite being displaced in the map.
scenarios.body: Blue To Blue, Mehmas Champion and Pearl Eye are all tagged as redistributed hold-up types who will not get their natural back-of-field berth, reducing the likelihood they finish with full impact; however, on the rare occasion soft ground and a strung-out field opens a late lane, any of them could be involved. This scenario carries the lowest weight precisely because the horses who would win it are not racing in their best role today.

watchPoints.text: Pomme Pomme sets the entire complexion of this race — if Clifford Lee allows a more genuine gallop on soft ground the prominent pack will be tested for stamina, but if the pace is too slow the closers will roll in from midfield; watch the early fractions closely.

Nightsinwhitesatin has finished second five times in six starts and the market will expect more of the same — if the prominent horses set too fast an early gallop on soft ground and the leader fades, this horse is the one most likely to finally get its head in front.

Storm Point's two wins have both come on soft or easy ground and the prominent style means it will be positioned to challenge in the straight — it arrives here well-prepared by Ed Walker (7 from 45 in 14 days) and the step to 12f on this surface looks an upgrade in suitability rather than a risk.

Blue To Blue, Mehmas Champion, Pearl Eye and High Point are all natural hold-up horses who cannot get to the rear of this field — their actual running positions will be further forward than their handlers would choose, which may compromise their ability to produce a late finish on tiring soft ground.

Night Patrol (90 days off) and Freddie Steady Go (82 days) both return from extended breaks — watch the paddock for condition and market moves; if either drifts in the market it suggests the stable is not expecting a forward showing first time up.
